title: 41. Evaluating the stability of 5-hydroxytryptamine in rumen fluid using an in vitro culturing approach.
content:
Abstract
5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) is an important signaling molecule that plays a significant role in regulating energy metabolism, gastrointestinal function, and cardiovascular regulation. Due to its role in gastrointestinal physiology and systemic signaling, feeding 5-HT represents a promising strategy to investigate its functions in ruminants. However, since there is minimal information on dosing via oral consumption, and that its stability in the rumen environment remains poorly characterized, the amounts needed to deliver an effective dose remain to be determined. In this context, we hypothesized that 5-HT can be metabolized by rumen microorganisms. Therefore, the objective of this pilot study was to measure the ruminal disappearance of 5-HT at varying ?show $132#?>concentrations using a rumen fluid-based in vitro batch-culture approach. Using a single cannulated steer as donor, duplicate cultures of ∼350 mL were supplemented with the following amounts of 5-HT: 0, 25, 75, or 125 mg. Cultures were incubated at 39 °C in a dry incubator on individual stir plates for continuous mixing. Samples (∼3 mL) were collected from each culture at 24 and 48 hours, then stored at -80 °C until analysis. Concentrations of 5-HT were quantified using an ELISA kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol. Data were analyzed by ANOVA for fixed effects of added 5-HT concentration and time, and means were separated by Tukey’s using R Software. Significance is declared at P ≤ 0.05. There was a main effect of added 5-HT, whereby 125 mg had a greater (P = 0.03) concentration in rumen fluid compared with 0 mg and 25 mg. There was no effect of time. While the highest concentration of 125 mg was greater than the two lowest concentrations, all concentrations had increasing levels of 5-HT, which remained throughout the 48 hr incubation. Therefore, it appears 5-HT is minimally metabolized by ruminal microorganisms. Characterizing 5-HT stability in the rumen is a critical first step in determining the possibility and dosage of dietary 5-HT utilization for reaching systemic circulation in cattle.
